title: Higher resolution
description: Draw the game at a larger size than the Switch's docked 1600x900. Costs GPU time and memory.

title: Graphics
description: Picture improvements. Anisotropic filtering keeps slanted textures such as the floor sharp into the distance. Texture detail uses sharper versions of every texture. Sharpen runs a light sharpening filter over the finished picture (the game already smooths edges with its own FXAA). Sharper shadows draws shadows at 2048 instead of the Switch's 1024. Reflections turns on the game's reflection setting, which the Switch build leaves off; it has not yet been seen on water.

title: Pulled-back camera
description: Move the in-game camera further from the hero to see more of the area. 1.0 is the game's own distance; 1.5 is a good start. Far values show more fog and may show unloaded edges.

title: Frame-rate counter
description: Show frames per second in the window's top-left corner, with the time each frame takes and how much of it went to the game's own work (CPU) and to drawing (GPU). It is also printed every ten seconds. Starting the game with D3_FPS=0 or 1 hides or shows it whatever this says.

title: Mouse
description: Use a mouse or trackpad alongside the controller. In menus, point at an entry to select it and click to choose it; a dialog's Accept and Cancel can be clicked. In the game, hold the left button to walk toward the pointer and hold the right button to use your primary skill (A), which also talks, opens and picks up.

title: Faster heroes
description: Multiply how fast heroes walk, run and sprint. 1.0 is the game's own speed.

title: Quality of life
description: Small changes for playing alone offline. Instant portal and identify skip the Town Portal channel, the wait when identifying an item and the Book of Cain's reading. Instant crafting skips the blacksmith's, the Mystic's and Kanai's Cube's waits. A free Cube still needs the materials to start a recipe but keeps them, and its gold; the item a recipe changes is still used up. Gem upgrades always succeed at the Urshi, or one upgrade takes a gem to rank 150. Any socket takes any gem, legendary gems included (a normal gem gives no bonus where the game has none for it). Any slot puts armour and jewellery in any armour or jewellery slot, so a ring can go on the head; weapons and off-hands stay in the hands. Unique-equipped legendaries, such as some rings, can be worn twice. Auto-pickup picks up legendary and set items when the hero walks over them, like gold.
labels: Instant identify and Book of Cain
Gem upgrades go straight to rank 150
Armour and jewellery in any slot
Wear two of a unique-equipped legendary

title: Seasons
description: Play a season offline, with its theme. The game makes that season active without Blizzard's servers, so the Season Journey and seasonal heroes are available, and turns on the season's theme, which applies to every hero, seasonal or not. Seasons 1 to 13 had no theme and their Season Journeys repeat in later seasons, so only the themed seasons are listed (season 23's theme, followers that fight like heroes, is built into 2.7.7). Seasonal heroes belong to the season they were made in: choosing another season ends the current one, and its seasonal heroes become normal heroes, as when a season ended online. With any theme on, the Altar of Rites (season 28) and Visions of Enmity portals (season 29) are on too, as in 2.7.7. Leaderboards and other online parts of seasons stay unavailable.
labels: Season 14: Season of Greed: double treasure goblins
Season 15: Boon of the Horadrim: double bounty caches
Season 16: Season of Grandeur: Royal Grandeur for everyone
Season 17: Season of Nightmares: Legacy of Nightmares for everyone
Season 18: Season of the Triune: Triune's Will
Season 19: Season of Eternal Conflict: Pandemonium
Season 22: Shades of the Nephalem: shadow clones, 4th cube slot
Season 23: Followers fight like heroes (built in)
Season 25: The Lords of Hell: soul shards
Season 28: Rites of Sanctuary: Altar of Rites
Season 29: Visions of Enmity: nesting portals

title: Season theme
description: Turn on one of 2.7.7's season themes. On the Switch these were switched on by Blizzard's servers for the length of a season, so offline none ever start. The chosen season's theme follows the season chosen above (seasons 14 to 37; season 23's theme, followers that fight like heroes, is built into 2.7.7). The theme applies to every hero, seasonal or not. With any theme on, the Altar of Rites (season 28) and Visions of Enmity portals (season 29) are on too, as in 2.7.7. With this mod on, the theme can also be changed while the game runs, to any season's, from the Season theme tab on this page or the designer menu's Game page (F8, with the developer tools); the game keeps the choice for the next start.
labels: None at the start (pick one in the game)
Shadow clones and a 4th cube slot (22, 33)

title: Challenge Rifts
description: Play Challenge Rifts without Blizzard's servers. Each challenge was two files the game downloaded every week; offline nothing arrives, so the game reads them from the rift_data folder in your game folder instead (challengerift_config.dat and challengerift_00.dat, challengerift_01.dat and so on). This project ships no challenge files: they hold the hero and account of the player who set the record. With Rotate, the challenges in the folder take turns, moving on each time you earn a reward; a number always plays that file. Challenge Rifts open once a hero on the account has cleared a solo Greater Rift (the Cheats tab's Greater rifts to 70 does that). Leaderboards stay unavailable.

title: Events
description: Turn on events Blizzard's servers ran. The Anniversary opens the Darkening of Tristram (its portal is in New Tristram) and gives the anniversary experience and magic-find buff; without this it still opens every January, from the game's own dates. The cow level is the game's not-a-cow-level easter egg. Double blood shards and double rift keystones double those rewards. Events apply to every hero. World bosses is our own event: every few minutes, while you are out of town and not in a rift, the game announces that a rift guardian waits somewhere else in your area, named on screen and in chat, and marks the spot on the minimap. The boss appears when you get there, then shows on the minimap as a quest monster; its death is announced too.

title: Minutes between world bosses
description: With the World bosses event on, how many minutes pass between one boss's death (or your leaving its area) and the next announcement.

title: Ancient items
description: Change how legendary and set items roll ancient, for drops, Kadala, crafting and Kanai's Cube alike. Only level-70 items can be ancient, as in the game. No primals keeps ancients but never rolls primal ancient; none turns ancients off; ancient or primal makes every level-70 legendary and set item that.

title: Drop level
description: Make monsters, chests and other world drops roll as if the area were this level, from 1 to 70: which items can drop, their stats and their level. 70 gives level-70 items from the start, which a low-level hero cannot wear yet. Kadala, crafting and the Cube keep their own levels.

title: Loot rules
description: Loosen the rules on what can drop. No Torment gate lets items the game keeps for Torment difficulties drop on every difficulty. No restrictions lets items kept for later acts, for rifts, for hardcore heroes or for a season's unlocks drop anywhere. Kadala legendaries makes every Kadala purchase a legendary or set item.

title: Deckard Cain's gems
description: Deckard Cain stands in New Tristram again, up and to the left of the waypoint, and sells custom legendary gems at their highest rank. Each adds a pylon's buff every so many kills while socketed. A hero holding one of these gems needs this mod on to load.

title: Corrupted legendaries
description: Kanai's Cube gains a Corrupt Legendary recipe: 1 legendary, 25 Death's Breath, 5 Forgotten Souls and 1 Corrupted Angel Flesh. The item gains a random boss skill (Diablo's Ring of Fire, Belial's lightning, Malthael's Mephisto skulls and more) that your hero sometimes casts on hit. Corrupting again rerolls the skill. A hero holding a corrupted item needs this mod on to load.

title: Cheats (for testing)
description: In the game, F1 raises your hero to level 70, F2 adds 100 paragon levels and F3 adds 10,000,000 gold. While the game runs, the Cheats tab on this page can also add gold, give you any item, unlock Kanai's Cube, count greater rifts up to a tier as cleared solo (which opens Challenge Rifts) and give Horadric Caches from any act (at the game's current difficulty). Changes are saved with your hero.

title: Start in a developer world
description: Skip the menus and start in one of the test worlds Blizzard's developers used, which ship with the game but can't be reached in normal play. The game makes a throwaway developer account and hero for it; your own heroes aren't loaded or changed. Turn it off to play normally again.

title: BlizzCon demo
description: Start the game the way the BlizzCon show-floor demo did: an offline party of level-70 demo heroes, and Continue goes straight into a Greater Rift. Your own heroes aren't changed. Turn it off to play normally again.

title: Developer views (F5-F9)
description: Hotkeys for views Blizzard's developers used, which the game still draws once switched on. F5: a fixed camera looking at your hero from the front, for screenshots (F5 again goes back). F6: the name of what you would attack, at the top of the screen (the release build shows it as a code). F7: the left stick's position and dead zone. F8: the designer menu, a developer menu left in the game; with Cheats on, its Character, Game and Quick Options entries work (Quest and Music only list things). F9: a free camera you fly with the controller (left stick moves, right stick turns, R/ZR up, L/ZL down, hold A for speed, hold B to go slowly); F9 again gives the controller back to your hero. It is also a photo mode: X hides the HUD, Plus pauses, d-pad up and down zoom, left or right toggles grayscale, Y takes a photo three times the window's size, and Minus takes a top-down map of the area you are looking at. Pictures go to Pictures/Diablo III.

title: Loose files and 1.0 arenas
description: Read game data files from the loose folder in your save folder before the game's archives, so files made outside the game can replace or add to its own. The 1.0 arenas tab uses it to play the PvP arenas of Diablo III's 2012 PC release, converted from your own 1.0 discs.
